THE OBJECT (FINDING-caiso242-offer-basis-identity-2026-09-03.md §5-§6, that session's strongest standing ask): three compounding defects delivered ONE EIA-923 row -- plant 55077 (Desert Star, NV) reporting 96.161 $/MMBtu on 5,234 MMBtu, 2.6 % of its own normal monthly volume, i.e. a fixed/reservation charge over a near-zero denominator and NOT a marginal delivered price -- to 2,445 MW of its CAISO neighbours (CC_REGULAR 55518 960.0, 55656 779.0, 55295 591.0 MW among them) at a marginal cost of ~$736/MWh for ALL 720 HOURS OF NOVEMBER 2025, the training window's worst C3a year. (D1) `state` was EMPTY on 100 % of the CAISO gas fleet (1,453/1,453 LP rows, 29,278 MW) because data/fleet/assembly.py::bins_to_fleet constructed every Generator WITHOUT a state argument -- the field defaults to '' and only the EIA-860 loader ever set it -- so the F923 fallback's documented state-first donor tier, THE ONLY TIER CARRYING A DISTINCT-REPORTER FLOOR (nearby_fuel_price_min_state_plants = 2, resolved on this lane), was skipped FLEET-WIDE on every plant-level fleet: CAISO, PJM, MISO, NYISO and NEISO alike, while the plant_level_fleet docstring claims the fleet 'retains its EIA plant code, plant group and state'. (D2) the zone tier it fell to carried NO reporter floor and its pool for those rows held EXACTLY ONE plant, 55077, whose price it returned to five decimals; the arithmetic proves the path -- NV's ten reporting gas plants that month are quantity-weighted at $3.54 and CA's at ~$4.5, so neither tier could produce 96.161 except from a pool of one. (D3) the source row itself. Reachable ONLY because the CAISO hub-basis overlay covers 9/12 months in 2025 (Sep/Oct/Nov open) against 12/12 in 2023-24 -- which is exactly why no keeper caught it. THE REPAIR, form (a)+(c), CHOSEN BY THE OWNER from the three shapes caiso-242 measured and deliberately did not select: ScenarioConfig.fleet_state_from_eia860 (form (c), the ROOT CAUSE of D1 -- bins_to_fleet stamps each generator's USPS state from the EIA-860 plant table, data/raw/eia-860/eia860_plant.parquet, so the designed tier order is reachable) and ScenarioConfig.nearby_fuel_price_zone_donor_guard (form (a), D2 -- the zone tier requires the SAME registered floor the state tier already carries). NO new constant, NO value chosen, ZERO FREE PARAMETERS (rule 21 [R-DOF]); both fields are ISO-GENERIC and default OFF, so every other ISO's keeper replays byte-identical, and the ARM is CAISO's alone (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]). Form (b), a volume-admissibility cut on F923 rows, was NOT armed: every candidate cut is a new parameter pair with no measured identification (rule 5 [R-NO-MAGIC]) and the tightest swept cut (quantity <= 2 % of the plant-year median) MISSES the very row that motivated it (55077-Nov is 2.62 %). MEASURED PRE-SOLVE, ZERO LP (_caiso243_fallback_footprint.json, _caiso243_gstruct_presolve.json): the coded mechanism reproduces the pre-registered footprint BYTE FOR BYTE in all five cases -- 1,364 rows / 25,526.9 MW of CA gas re-tier onto the 6-reporter CA state mean in Sep/Oct/Nov 2025 ONLY (Nov capacity-weighted 13.48 -> 4.38 $/MMBtu, fuel-side mc 119.1 -> 42.5 $/MWh; the 96.161 rows to 4.38; NP15/LA_BASIN/ZP26 move by < $1/MMBtu), ZERO non-gas rows, and ZERO rows in 2023 and 2024. EVERY PRE-REGISTERED GATE PASSES (PRECOMMIT-caiso243-f923-fallback-guard-2026-09-04.md §5, plus its ADDENDUM). G-CTRL is FORM 2 -- caiso-240's dispatch identity in a measured-inert year, which binds here under the owner's caiso-241 §B2 carve-out ('an arm with even one inert year takes the caiso-240 dispatch-identity leg and spends nothing') and was the owner's explicit choice: NO CONTROL SOLVE WAS SPENT, and 2023 and 2024 reproduce the keeper EXACTLY -- 0.000 TWh in every class and 0.000 $/MWh, not merely inside the 0.001 TWh tolerance. P-5 registered that CT_PEAKER would fall AND that imports would fall by LESS than CC_REGULAR rises; its first leg holds (CT_PEAKER -0.030 TWh) and its SECOND LEG IS FALSIFIED -- imports fall 0.473 TWh against CC_REGULAR's +0.442 TWh rise, so the repaired domestic capacity displaces slightly MORE import energy than it adds to its own class. The displacement is the structural signature caiso-242 §2.5 predicted (an over-priced domestic offer surface makes imports win hours peakers and CCs should win), measured for the first time. P-4 holds: CC_REGULAR's November rise is +396 MW (< 500) and +0.442 TWh (< 0.5), so caiso-242's against-interest reading -- capability removed and cost misallocated WITHIN the class, not a class-level generation hole -- survives its own test. The object, its form, the inert years and every gate survive the correction; the numbers moved at the second digit. The 2025 overlay coverage gap (9/12) stays open. And the CT_PEAKER volume object is untouched. CROSS-ISO, MEASURED AND FILED AS ASKS, NEVER ARMED (rule 25): PJM carries 4 anomalous rows across 3 plants (max 191.64 $/MMBtu) and MISO 12 across 9 (max 198.46, the largest exposure of the six), both with NO hub overlay -- so their fallback layer is live in all 36 months and their state tier is equally empty; NYISO and NEISO have none; ERCOT runs neither flag.
